# tfhunter

The goal of **tfhunter** is to identify transcription factors (TFs) from
protein sequence data of any eukaryotic species and classify them into
families using the classification scheme of
[CIS-BP](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2014.08.009). Plant TFs can also
be classified into families and subfamilies using the classification
schemes implemented in [PlantTFDB](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkw982)
and [TAPscan](https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.17184), and into
structure-based families, classes, and superclasses as in
[Plant-TFClass](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tplants.2023.06.023).
Mammalian TFs can be classified into structure-based superclasses,
classes, and families as in
[TFClass](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkx987).

**tfhunter** is the successor of the Bioconductor package
[planttfhunter](https://bioconductor.org/packages/planttfhunter).

## Installation instructions

Get the latest stable `R` release from
[CRAN](http://cran.r-project.org/). Then install **tfhunter** from
[Bioconductor](http://bioconductor.org/) using the following code:

\
`if`` ``(``!`[`requireNamespace`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/ns-load.html)`(``"BiocManager"``, quietly ``=`` ``TRUE``)``)`` ``{`\
`    `[`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(``"BiocManager"``)`\
`}`\
\
`BiocManager``::`[`install`](https://bioconductor.github.io/BiocManager/reference/install.html)`(``"tfhunter"``)`

Or the development version from
[GitHub](https://github.com/almeidasilvaf/tfhunter) with:

\
`BiocManager``::`[`install`](https://bioconductor.github.io/BiocManager/reference/install.html)`(``"almeidasilvaf/tfhunter"``)`

**tfhunter**.

Please note that the **tfhunter** project was only made possible thanks
to many other R and bioinformatics software authors, which are cited
either in the vignettes and/or the paper(s) describing this package.

## Code of Conduct

Please note that the **tfhunter** project is released with a
[Contributor Code of
Conduct](http://bioconductor.org/about/code-of-conduct/). By
contributing to this project, you agree to abide by its terms.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`annotate_domains()`](annotate_domains.md) : Annotate protein
  sequences with domains used for TF classification

- [`cisbp_scheme`](cisbp_scheme.md) : Data frame of CIS-BP's TF family
  classification scheme

- [`classify_tfs()`](classify_tfs.md) : Identify TFs and classify them
  in families

- [`get_tf_counts()`](get_tf_counts.md) :

  Get TF frequencies for each species as a `SummarizedExperiment` object

- [`gsu`](gsu.md) : Protein sequences of the algae species Galdieria
  sulphuraria

- [`gsu_annotation`](gsu_annotation.md) :

  Domain annotation for the algae species Galdieria sulphuraria The data
  set was created using the function
  [`annotate_domains()`](../reference/annotate_domains.md).

- [`hmmer_is_installed()`](hmmer_is_installed.md) : Check if HMMER is
  installed

- [`human_tfs`](human_tfs.md) : Curated human transcription factors and
  their classifications

- [`list_schemes()`](list_schemes.md) : List available TF classification
  schemes

- [`planttfclass_scheme`](planttfclass_scheme.md) : Correspondence table
  between TAPscan and Plant-TFClass

- [`planttfdb_scheme`](planttfdb_scheme.md) : Data frame of PlantTFDB's
  TF family classification scheme

- [`tap_class`](tap_class.md) : Classes of transcription-associated
  proteins (TAPs) in TAPscan

- [`tapscan_scheme`](tapscan_scheme.md) : Data frame of TAPscan's
  classification scheme

- [`tfclass_scheme`](tfclass_scheme.md) : Correspondence table between
  CIS-BP and TFClass
